final_response:
{
  "instruction_blocks": [
    "Translate the requirements into a complete Cedar policy set. Requirements determine authorization semantics; the schema determines available types and representations. Descriptions of people, resources, attributes, and context do not themselves grant access or impose conditions. Do not infer ownership, assignment, membership, role, or context restrictions merely from available fields. Do not infer permission from the absence of a prohibition.",
    "For each action, distinguish affirmative permissions, necessary conditions, prohibitions, exceptions, and required successful cases. Preserve the direction of each implication: 'only when' establishes a necessary condition, not a universal grant to everyone satisfying it. Preserve any permission actually stated in the same sentence. Identify who receives each permission and under which circumstances; do not enlarge that population through a restriction or exception.",
    "Read related statements together. Repeated restrictions usually describe one condition, not additional permission paths. Combine simultaneously required conditions with AND and alternative ways to satisfy the same condition with OR. An explicit exception qualifies the restriction it addresses, even when an earlier sentence states that restriction without qualification. Preserve all unrelated requirements.",
    "Keep exceptions local. Waiving a prohibition or condition does not independently authorize the request, expand an existing grant, or waive another restriction. A statement that a request must succeed supplies an affirmative authorization obligation for its stated population and circumstances. Preserve those limits: a successful case for one role does not authorize other roles merely because they share restrictions. Ensure required successful cases have an applicable permit and escape every applicable forbid.",
    "Scope every permit and forbid to the stated actions, principal populations, resources, and conditions. Roles may overlap; evaluate their predicates independently. An applicable forbid overrides every permit, including permits obtained through another role. Use forbids for explicit vetoes with their exact scope and exceptions; do not turn an absent grant into a blanket veto. Keep action rules separate when their conditions differ. Leave requests without authorization denied by default.",
    "Use exact schema identifiers and capitalization. Preserve strings, entity references, sets, numbers, and extension types. Distinguish role membership from ownership, set containment from entity hierarchy membership, and equality from ancestry. Use schema-supported Cedar syntax, operators, entity literals, and extension methods. Guard optional attributes with has before accessing them in a logically protective expression. Return only the policy JSON required by the public instructions."
  ],
  "input_order": [
    "requirements",
    "schema"
  ],
  "checklist": [
    "Every stated permission and required successful case retains its intended scope.",
    "Necessary conditions, exception paths, and sufficient authorization remain distinct.",
    "No schema field has introduced an unstated grant or restriction.",
    "Exceptions remove only their qualified obstacles.",
    "Overlapping roles preserve every applicable veto without inventing new vetoes.",
    "All actions, types, optional guards, Cedar expressions, and the final JSON format are consistent."
  ]
}
